---
title: "The Limit Order Book — Review"
---

## Trading Mechanisms

| Mechanism | Counterparty | Profit | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OTC / Market Maker** | Market Maker | Bid-ask spread | Inventory |
| **LOB** (Limit Order Book) | Other participants | — | Opportunity |

> **LOB** $\mathcal{L}(t)$ = set of **active** orders (submitted, not executed, not cancelled) at time $t$.

---

## Key Definitions

An order: $x = (p_x,\ w_x,\ t_x)$ — price, size, timestamp

| Symbol | Definition | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| $b(t)$ | **Bid** — best buy price | $\max_{x \in B(t)} p_x$ |
| $a(t)$ | **Ask** — best sell price | $\min_{x \in A(t)} p_x$ |
| $s(t)$ | **Spread** | $a(t) - b(t) \geq 0$ |
| $m(t)$ | **Mid-price** | $\dfrac{a(t)+b(t)}{2}$ |
| $\delta^x$ | **Relative Price** | $b(t)-p_x$ (buy) / $p_x - a(t)$ (sell) |
| $\pi$ | **Tick** — smallest price increment | — |
| $N^b(p,t)$ | **Bid depth** | $\sum_{\{x \in B(t)\mid\delta^x=p\}} w_x$ |
| $N^a(p,t)$ | **Ask depth** | $\sum_{\{x \in A(t)\mid\delta^x=p\}} w_x$ |

---

## Order Types

| Type | Condition (buy) | Execution | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Limit Order** | $p_x \leq b(t)$ or inside the spread | ❌ Deferred | Non-execution (opportunity) |
| **Market Order** | $p_x \geq a(t)$ | ✅ Immediate | Unfavorable price |

⚠️ **Fundamental arbitrage:** better price ↔ non-execution risk

---

## LOB Evolution — 3 cases (buy)

| Condition | Type | Effect on $b(t)$ |
|---|---|---|
| $p_x \leq b(t)$ | Limit | Unchanged |
| $b(t) < p_x < a(t)$ | Limit | $b(t) \uparrow$ towards $p_x$ |
| $p_x \geq a(t)$ | Market | Execution at best ask |

---

## Priority Rules

| Rule | Criterion 1 | Criterion 2 | Favors |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Price-Time** | Best price | FIFO | Early orders |
| **Pro-Rata** | Best price | $w / \sum w$ | Large orders |
| **Price-Size** | Best price | Largest $w$ | Large orders |

---

## Visibility

- **Standard LOB**: published by most exchanges
- **Iceberg Orders**: partially hidden size
- **Dark pools**: opaque LOB, fully hidden orders

⚠️ A transparent LOB provides access to far more than $a(t)$ and $b(t)$ — but the dynamics remain poorly understood.

---

## Empirical Facts

| Property | Observation |
|---|---|
| **Order Size** | Uniform + concentrated on round values |
| **Relative Price** $\delta$ | Power law, **fat tails** |
| **Cancellations** | **70–80 %** of orders cancelled |
| **Depth** | Fat-tailed distribution |
| **Price Impact** | $I(\|w\|)$ **concave** in $\|w\|$ |

> **Permanent impact** ← information transmitted to other traders or triggered order cascade.

> **Master Curve** (Lillo et al.): after normalization by market capitalization → universal power law.

---

## Maslov Model

**Algorithm (at each step):**

- Buyer or seller with $p = 0{,}5$
- Prob. $1-r$ → **market order** $(bid/ask,\ \sigma,\ t_x)$
- Prob. $r$ → **limit order** $p_x = p' \mp k$ ($k$ random, $p'$ = last price)
- No cancellation

**Key results:**

| Property | Value / Observation |
|---|---|
| Increment distribution | **Non-Gaussian**, fat tails |
| Volatility | **Clustering** |
| Hurst exponent $H$ | $\approx 1/4$ (vs $1/2$ for random walk) |
| Autocorrelation | **Negative** (anti-persistence) |

> $H < 0{,}5$ → **mean-reverting** (anti-persistent) · $H = 0{,}5$ → random walk · $H > 0{,}5$ → trending

## Relations between concepts

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Order submitted] --> B{Matched ?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Market Order]
  B -- No --> D[Limit Order]
  D --> E[Active LOB]
  E --> F{Cancelled ?}
  F -- 70-80% --> G[Cancellation]
  F -- 20-30% --> H[Execution]
```

---

## Pitfalls to avoid ⚠️

- $s(t) \geq 0$ **always** — if $a(t) < b(t)$, a match would have occurred
- Limit order ≠ guaranteed execution → **opportunity risk**
- Price impact **concave**: doubling $|w|$ does **not** double the impact
- Maslov: homogeneous model → for heterogeneity → **ABM** (Agent-Based Models)
- Dark pools: opacity ≠ guaranteed efficiency
